```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Primary Hub"
node hubbackup "Backup Hub"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary "Primary WAN"
edge branch hubbackup "Backup WAN"
```

This topology figure models the branch office network you described:

- **Two access switches** (access1, access2) sit at the branch and connect to the branch router
- **The branch router** is the convergence point, connecting the local access layer to the WAN
- **Two regional hub routers** receive traffic from the branch: the primary hub carries the preferred WAN link, and the backup hub carries the diverse-path failover link

The labels on the WAN edges (`Primary WAN` and `Backup WAN`) make the redundancy strategy explicit without overstuffing node labels. The topology genre is experimental (EXPERIMENTAL), so rendering behavior may vary across versions before v1.0.
